schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT A1.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (A1.FIRST_LOGIN + 1) = A2.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/ COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS A1 JOIN ACTIVITY AS A2 ON A1.PLAYER_ID = A2.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY A1.FIRST_LOGIN
q2: WITH T1 AS (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS INSTALL_DT FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID), T2 AS (SELECT T1.INSTALL_DT, T1.PLAYER_ID, A.PLAYER_ID AS DAY_ONE_ID FROM T1 LEFT JOIN ACTIVITY A ON T1.PLAYER_ID = A.PLAYER_ID AND T1.INSTALL_DT = A.EVENT_DATE - 1 ) SELECT INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS , ROUND(IFNULL(COUNT(DISTINCT DAY_ONE_ID)/COUNT(DISTINCT PLAYER_ID), 0), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM T2 GROUP BY INSTALL_DT

counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTIVITY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE, DEVICE_ID, GAMES_PLAYED) VALUES (1, '2023-01-01', 101, 5);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses a JOIN operation to match players' first login with their next day's activity, while Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN and a conditional COUNT to achieve the same goal. The difference arises when there are players who do not have an event on the day immediately following their first login.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include a player who has an event on their first login date but no event on the day immediately following it. This scenario will cause Q1 to count this player as a retention, while Q2 will not.
